SABIC} Office of the City Legal Officer 3/'F Bacolod City Government Center Circumferential Road, Bacolod City 6100 Dear Atty. Sabig: 'I'his is in reference to your letter dated IO November 2017 requesting this Department's legal opinion relative to the application of the provision of DILG-DTI-DICT Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 01, s. 2016, 30 August 2016, re: Revised Standards in Processing Business Permits and Licenses in all Cities and Municipalities. In the said letter, you raised the following queries, to wit: 2. Whether or not the City Mayor may validly revoke the business permit issued for the failure of UVITOP to submit an Order from the Intestate Court appro ving the Contract of Lease; Whether or not the City may validly refuse the renewal of the said business permit for 2018 in case UNIT'OP fails to submit the Order from the Intestate Court approving the Lease Contract; It can be gleaned from your letter that these issues were primarily anchored on the validity of the Contract of Lease between the Partnership Sy Yong Hu & Sons, et. al., and IiN/TOP General Merchandise, Inc., because it will be the basis for the issuance Of the business permit to be issued by the City of Bacolod. It was also stated in the letter that the issue on the validity of the Lease Contract is now with the Regional Trial Court Branch 46, Bacolod City (RTC) together with the intestate proceedings of the deceased Sy Yong Elu. Therefore, this issue is considered justiciable in nature. Based on your representation of the herein facts, please be informed that this Department is prohibited from giving its opinion on the validity of the lease contract for purposes of business permit application as the same is sanctioned by Memorandum Order No. 2010-021 dated 17 September 2010, which provides: "Xxx all concerned are hereby advised that the Department shall not act on queries of the föllowing kinds, to wit: Supplement to Memorandum Order No. 2010-01 (Requests for [egal Opinion from the DILG Central Office) dated March 2010

I. Those containing facts that are justiciable in nature. Justiciable issues are those that require adjudication by the courts of law as to who between the opposing parties have the better right over a given contro versy,• However, for purposes of academic discussions only, please be reminded that "permits and licenses are issued Tor regulatory purposes and under certain condition upon which they are issued pursuant to a law or ordinance, the entitlement thereof is not a matter of right but a privilege, and neither is it a property. A license or a permit is not a contract between the sovereignty and the licensee or permitee, and is not a property in the constitutional sense, as to which the constitutional proscription against impairment of the obligation of contracts may extend. A license is rather in the nature ofa special privilege, ofa permission or authority to do what is within its terms. It is not in any way vested, permanent or absolute. Hence, it is necessary to determine first the validity of the contract of lease before the City of Bacolod can decide on whether or not it can issue a business permit for 2018 or revoke the business license already issued to the UNITOP. To reiterate, the issuance of the business permit by the City of Bacolod depends on the validity of the herein contract. With this, the Department is proscribed to give its opinion on the herein issue as the determination of the validity of the contract is justiciable in nature and already pending in RTC Branch 46, Bacolod City. Hence, this Department will defer to the pronouncement of the competent Court on its validity. Now, aside from your office's letter request, this Department also received these communications: (a) Letter dated 5 December 2017 from Ms. Yolanda KS Lee providing some clarification in connection with the aforesaid request for legal opinion; and (b) Letters dated 18 December 2017 and 16 December 2017 from John Keng Seng a.k.a. John Sy submitting supplemental documents to support the revocation and/or non-renewal of the Business Permit issued to Unitop General Merchandise, Inc. Hence, insofar as the issue of revocation of the business permit already issued is concerned, vv'e shall render a resounding opinion. The instant question is whether or not the chief executive can be compelled to revoke or disapprove renewal of a business permit based on a fact that the lease contract submitted as one of the requirements for its issuance was not signed by the real owner of the leased premises. The Department leans on an adversative position. 2 Acebedo Optical Company, Inc. vs CA, GR No. 100152, 31 March 2000; DILG Legal Opinion No. 33, s. 201 1

gection of R.A. 7160. otherwise known as the "Local Government Code", all local chief executives are vested with authority to "issue licenses and permits and suspend or revoke the same for any violation of the conditions upon which said licenses or permits had been issued, pursuant to Ia w or ordinance 't (Emphasis Supplied) It is clear, therefore, that business permits can be revoked by the City Mayor thru its Building Permits and Licensing Office (BPLO) if there is violation or non-compliance by the grantee of the requirements set forth by law or ordinance for its issuance. The case of Hon. Alfredo Lim and Rafaelito Garayblas, vs. The Court of Appeals, et.al•/ discussed as follows: It is clear that the power of the mayor to issue business licenses and permits necessarily includes the corollary power to suspend, revoke or even refuse to issue the same. However, the power to suspend or revoke these licenses and permits is expressly premised on the violation of the conditions of these permits and licenses. The laws specifically refer to the violation of the condition(s) on which the licenses and permits were issued. Similarly, the power to refuse to issue such licenses and permits is premised on non- compliance with the prerequisites for the issuance of such licenses and permits. The mayor must observe due process in exercising these powers, which means that the mayor must give the applicant or licensee notice and opportunity to be heard. Verily, the power to suspend or revoke licenses and permits should be based upon violation of the condition/s upon which said licenses or permits had been issued. At this point, it is relevant to state that the most significant rationale behind the submission of title of ownership or a lease contract for business licensing purposes is only to prove that the applicant is/will be existing as a legitimate business enterprise. Herein, the issue revolves on who is the real owner of the building occupied by Unitop General Merchandise, Inc. which relatively boils down to identifying the real lessor insofar as the lease contract is concerned. A sensible deduction therefrom is that the proper remedy of the party claiming actual ownership of the leased premises is for him to be substituted as the true/actual lessor and the real party-in-interest to the lease contract. Conversely, if the lease agreement is to be terminated, Unitop General Merchandise, Inc. has the option to transfer to another location within the same LGU's territorial jurisdiction without in any way affecting the validity of their business permit as it can update the records of the Business Licensing and Processing Office whenever necessary. For that reason, a remedy of requesting for the suspension/revocation of a business permit is undoubtedly illogical. 3 G.R. No. 111397, August 12, 2002.

Mainly, said controversy on the lessor's title to the leased property does not constitute a lessee's violation of the conditions upon which the business permit was issued. More so that the issuance ofa business permit by the Local Chief Executive is between the Local Government and the grantee which is dependent upon the latter's compliance of the requirements prescribed by law or ordinance, as the case may be. to: 2. In closing, the Department's recommendation is for the City Legal Office of Bacolod Inform both John Sy and Yolanda Lee, that the dispute between them concerning their conflicting claims to the property leased by Unitop General Merchandise, Inc., is not a ground for the revocation of the business permit issued by the City Government to Unitop General Merchandise, Inc.; and Advise both John Sy and Yolanda Lee to secure judicial declaration as to who the real owner of the subject leased property and furnish both Unitop General Merchandise, Inc. and the Business Licensing and Processing Office (BPLO) of Bacolod City with a copy of the same. This will aid the BPLO in its assessment as to the veracity of the lease contract to be submitted by Unitop General Merchandise, Inc. for purposes of business permit renewal. We hope to have fully guided you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHOR F THE SECRETARY: AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary USLG 2018-02-1 •00 JOHN KENG SENG a.k.a.
